## Multivariate Real Data Analysis: Data Preparation

Run the code below to prepare the dataset for the multivariate multinomial probit model. First, load the response-specific predictor matrices (X_ML.RData and X_AD.RData) obtained from the preceding univariate real data analysis. 
```{r}

data <- read.csv(file.path(path, "Real_data.csv"),check.names = FALSE)

response <- data[, c("Mental_illness", "Alcohol_&_drug_abuse")]

X <- data[, !names(data) %in% c("Mental_illness", "Alcohol_&_drug_abuse")]

X<-covariate_processing(X)

# Add intercept
X <- cbind(Intercept = 1, X)

# Response-specific covariate sets
# ---- Covariates for response Mental illness ----
load("X_ML.RData") # you need to get this from the real_data_univariate file
x <-X_ML

# ---- Covariates for response Alcohol and drug abuse ----
load("X_AD.RData") # you need to get this from the real_data_univariate file
xx <-X_AD



y12 <- response

# Recode ordinal outcomes: 1/2 → 1, 3 → 2, 4 → 3, else → 4
y12 <- apply(y12, 2, function(x) {
  ifelse(x %in% c(1, 2), 1,
         ifelse(x == 3, 2,
                ifelse(x == 4, 3, 4)))
})

category_name <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)


y1  <- y12[, 1]
y2  <- y12[, 2]
y <- c(y1, y2)


# Build datasets and remove missing rows
data1 <- data.frame(y1, x)
data2 <- data.frame(y2, xx)

# Combine and drop NA rows
data <- na.omit(data.frame(data1, data2)) # remove the missing values

# Split back into two matrices
end_col <- which(colnames(data) == "y2")

data1 <- as.matrix(data[, 1:(end_col - 1)])
data2 <- as.matrix(data[, end_col:ncol(data)])


# Final response and predictor matrices
y1 <- data1[, 1]
X1 <- data1[, -1]

y2 <- data2[, 1]
X2 <- data2[, -1]


y12 <- cbind(y1, y2)



# Compute number of categories for each response
k1 <- length(sort(unique(y12[, 1]), decreasing = TRUE))
k2 <- length(sort(unique(y12[, 2]), decreasing = TRUE))



big_x1<-diag((k1-1)) %x% X1 
big_x2<-diag((k2-1)) %x% X2 

x_tilda<-rbind(cbind(big_x1,matrix(0,ncol=ncol(big_x2),nrow=nrow(big_x1))),cbind(matrix(0,ncol=ncol(big_x1),nrow=nrow(big_x2)),big_x2))



```




## Reproduce Table 8: Posterior Estimates of Cross-Response Correlations
Run the code below to fit the multivariate multinomial probit model using the joint \(S\) method and reproduce Table 8. The code obtains posterior samples of the regression coefficients and covariance parameters, then calculates the posterior medians and 95% highest posterior density (HPD) interval widths for the cross-response correlation parameters between mental illness and alcohol and drug abuse.

```{r}

#################################
# Code to generate Table 8
#################################

nit=50000
nmc=50000
nthin=10
tau2<-0.025^2
lamda2=10
proposal_step=.1

set.seed(12345)
MCMC_Joint_S_bivariate_real<- run_multinomial_bivariate_Joint_S_mcmc(X1,X2,y1, y2,
                                                      nit=nit, nmc=nmc, nthin=nthin,
                                                      tau2=tau2,lamda2=lamda2,
                                                      proposal_step=proposal_step)

save(MCMC_Joint_S_bivariate_real,file = file.path(path, "MCMC_Joint_S_bivariate_real.RData"))


Joint_S_beta<-MCMC_Joint_S_bivariate_real$beta_final_vector
Joint_S_sigma<-MCMC_Joint_S_bivariate_real$sigma2_final
Joint_S_S<-MCMC_Joint_S_bivariate_real$S_final
Joint_S_R<-MCMC_Joint_S_bivariate_real$R_final






###  Compute posterior medians & HPDIs for the full R matrix
R_median <- apply(Joint_S_R, c(2,3), median)

R_hdi <- apply(Joint_S_R, c(2,3), function(x) hdi(x, ci = 0.95))
R_low  <- R_hdi[1, , ]
R_high <- R_hdi[2, , ]


R12_med  <- R_median[1:3, 1:3]
R12_low  <- R_low[1:3, 1:3]
R12_high <- R_high[1:3, 1:3]



###  Create formatted cells "median (width)"
fmt <- function(m, lo, hi){
  width <- round(hi - lo, 2)
  paste0(round(m, 2), " (", width, ")")
}

Table_cells <- matrix("", nrow = 3, ncol = 3)

for(i in 1:3){
  for(j in 1:3){
    Table_cells[i,j] <- fmt(R12_med[i,j], R12_low[i,j], R12_high[i,j])
  }
}



Final_df <- data.frame(
  Alcohol_Category = c("Category 1","Category 2","Category 3"),
  Category1 = Table_cells[,1],
  Category2 = Table_cells[,2],
  Category3 = Table_cells[,3]
)

kable(
  Final_df,
  align = "lccc",
  col.names = c("Alcohol & Drug Abuse ", "Category 1", "Category 2", "Category 3"),
  caption = "Posterior median and 95% HPD interval width for cross-correlation entries in R12 matrix"
) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Mental Illness" = 3)) %>%
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)


```






## Reproduce Table 9: Model Comparison Using Different Covariance Structures
Run the code below to reproduce Table 9 by evaluating the multivariate multinomial probit model under different covariance structures. The code calculates the 95% highest posterior density (HPD) interval of the log-likelihood, Bayesian Predictive Information Criterion (BPIC), and Widely Applicable Information Criterion (WAIC) for the full covariance matrix. To obtain the corresponding results for the zero cross-covariance matrix, activate line 346 in Bivariate_joint_S.R; for the diagonal covariance matrix, activate lines 351–352. Rerun the joint \(S\) MCMC analysis and repeat the calculations.

```{r}

#################################
# Code to generate Table 9
#################################


category_position_y12 = as.list(rep(NA,k1*k2))
dim(category_position_y12) = c(k1,k2)
for (i in 1:k1)
{
  for (j in 1:k2)
  {
    category_position_y12[[i,j]] = which(apply(y12, 1, function(a) { max(abs(a - c(i,j)))} )== 0) ## which observations have 1st y category = i AND 2nd y category = j
  }
}

###Full matrix : HPDI of log-likelihood, BPIC ###
set.seed(12345)
loglikelihood_Joint_S <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(Joint_S_beta)), function(i) {
  X_BETA_tilda<-colSums( t(x_tilda)*  Joint_S_beta[, i] )        
  X_BETA<-matrix( X_BETA_tilda, ncol= (k1-1)+(k2-1) ) 
  unlist(log_likelihood_mnp_2response(category_position_y12,k1,k2,mu1=X_BETA[,1:(k1-1)],mu2=X_BETA[,((k1):ncol(X_BETA))],Joint_S_sigma[,, i],r=250,Halton_choice=FALSE)[2])
})



beta_bar<-( apply(Joint_S_beta,1,mean) )
sigma_bar<-apply(Joint_S_sigma, c(1,2), mean)
X_BETA_tilda<-colSums(t(x_tilda)* c(beta_bar))   
X_BETA_bar<-matrix( X_BETA_tilda,  ncol= (k1-1)+(k2-1) )


set.seed(12345)
D_theta_bar<- -2*unlist(log_likelihood_mnp_2response(category_position_y12,k1,k2,mu1=X_BETA_bar[,1:(k1-1)],mu2=X_BETA_bar[,((k1):ncol(X_BETA_bar))],sigma_bar,r=250,Halton_choice=FALSE)[2])
D_bar<- -2*mean(loglikelihood_Joint_S)
p_D <- D_bar - D_theta_bar
BPIC <- D_bar + 2 * p_D




# WAIC
set.seed(12345)

n_draws <- ncol(Joint_S_beta)
n_obs   <- nrow(X1)

loglikelihood_Joint_S_WAIC <- t(
  vapply(
    seq_len(n_draws),
    FUN.VALUE = numeric(n_obs),
    FUN = function(i) {
      
      X_BETA_tilda <- colSums(
        t(x_tilda) * Joint_S_beta[, i]
      )
      
      X_BETA <- matrix(
        X_BETA_tilda,
        nrow = n_obs,
        ncol = (k1 - 1) + (k2 - 1)
      )
      
      log_likelihood_mnp_2response_WAIC(
        pos_y = category_position_y12,
        k1 = k1,
        k2 = k2,
        mu1 = X_BETA[, seq_len(k1 - 1), drop = FALSE],
        mu2 = X_BETA[
          ,
          k1:(k1 + k2 - 2),
          drop = FALSE
        ],
        sigma = Joint_S_sigma[, , i],
        r = 250,
        Halton_choice = FALSE
      )$observation_log_likelihood
    }
  )
)



print(hdi(loglikelihood_Joint_S))
print(BPIC)

loo::waic(loglikelihood_Joint_S_WAIC)


# To calculate HPDI log-likelihood and BPIC for (zero matrix) activate line 346 in Bivariate_joint_S file and rerun line 109 and repeat the process same as full matrix

# To calculate HPDI log-likelihood and BPIC for (diagonal matrix ) activate line 351-352 in Bivariate_joint_S file and rerun line 109 and repeat the process same as full matrix

```





## Reproduce Table 7: Cross-Validation Results for the Multivariate Model

Run the code below to reproduce Table 7, which compares the observed category proportions with their corresponding 95% highest posterior density (HPD) predictive intervals for mental illness and alcohol and drug abuse under the multivariate multinomial probit model. The analysis considers covariate combinations with at least 30 observations and calculates the marginal predictive probabilities for each response from the joint posterior predictive probabilities. The results are presented separately for both responses.
```{r}
############################################################
# TABLE 7: Cross-validation for the bivariate MNP model
# Joint S covariance update
############################################################

# MCMC settings
nit <- 50000
nmc <- 50000
nthin <- 10
tau2 <- 0.025^2
lamda2 <- 10
proposal_step <- 0.1

# Model dimensions
p1 <- ncol(X1)
p2 <- ncol(X2)

k1 <- length(unique(y1))
k2 <- length(unique(y2))

# Complete dataset from the preceding preparation step
full_data <- data.frame(
  y1 = y1,
  X1,
  y2 = y2,
  X2,
  check.names = FALSE
)

x1_full <- as.matrix(X1)
x2_full <- as.matrix(X2)

############################################################
# 1. Identify eligible covariate combinations
############################################################

unq_row_of_X_y1 <- unique(x1_full)
unq_row_of_X_y2 <- unique(x2_full)

target_count <- 30

# Count observations for each unique combination
count_combinations <- function(X, patterns) {
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(patterns)), function(i) {
    sum(
      rowSums(
        sweep(X, 2, patterns[i, ], FUN = "-") == 0
      ) == ncol(X)
    )
  }, numeric(1))
}

count_y1 <- count_combinations(
  x1_full, unq_row_of_X_y1
)

count_y2 <- count_combinations(
  x2_full, unq_row_of_X_y2
)

# Retain combinations with at least 30 observations
unq_row_of_X_y1 <- unq_row_of_X_y1[
  count_y1 >= target_count, , drop = FALSE
]

unq_row_of_X_y2 <- unq_row_of_X_y2[
  count_y2 >= target_count, , drop = FALSE
]

############################################################
# 2. Construct cross-validation jobs
############################################################

cv_jobs <- c(
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(unq_row_of_X_y1)), function(i) {
    list(
      response = 1L,
      target_row = unq_row_of_X_y1[i, ]
    )
  }),
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(unq_row_of_X_y2)), function(i) {
    list(
      response = 2L,
      target_row = unq_row_of_X_y2[i, ]
    )
  })
)

############################################################
# 3. Cross-validation using the existing MCMC function
############################################################

estimated_PP_list <- vector("list", length(cv_jobs))
test_Y_list <- vector("list", length(cv_jobs))

cv_response_list <- integer(length(cv_jobs))
cv_target_row_list <- vector("list", length(cv_jobs))

for (cv in seq_along(cv_jobs)) {

  job <- cv_jobs[[cv]]
  target_row <- job$target_row

  ##########################################################
  # Determine held-out observations
  ##########################################################

  if (job$response == 1L) {

    index <- which(
      rowSums(
        sweep(x1_full, 2, target_row, "-") == 0
      ) == p1
    )

  } else {

    index <- which(
      rowSums(
        sweep(x2_full, 2, target_row, "-") == 0
      ) == p2
    )
  }

  ##########################################################
  # Split the complete bivariate dataset
  ##########################################################

  train_data <- full_data[-index, , drop = FALSE]
  test_data  <- full_data[index, , drop = FALSE]

  n_test <- nrow(test_data)

  # Training predictors and responses
  x1_train <- as.matrix(
    train_data[, 2:(p1 + 1), drop = FALSE]
  )

  x2_train <- as.matrix(
    train_data[, (p1 + 3):ncol(train_data),
               drop = FALSE]
  )

  y1_train <- as.numeric(train_data$y1)
  y2_train <- as.numeric(train_data$y2)

  # Test predictors and responses
  x1_test <- as.matrix(
    test_data[, 2:(p1 + 1), drop = FALSE]
  )

  x2_test <- as.matrix(
    test_data[, (p1 + 3):ncol(test_data),
              drop = FALSE]
  )

  y1_test <- as.numeric(test_data$y1)
  y2_test <- as.numeric(test_data$y2)

  ##########################################################
  # Fit the bivariate multinomial probit model
  ##########################################################

  set.seed(12345 + cv)

  MCMC_Joint_S <- run_multinomial_bivariate_Joint_S_mcmc(
    X1 = x1_train,
    X2 = x2_train,
    y1 = y1_train,
    y2 = y2_train,
    nit = nit,
    nmc = nmc,
    nthin = nthin,
    tau2 = tau2,
    lamda2 = lamda2,
    proposal_step = proposal_step
  )

  ##########################################################
  # Extract posterior samples
  ##########################################################

  Joint_S_beta <- MCMC_Joint_S$beta_final_vector
  Joint_S_sigma <- MCMC_Joint_S$sigma2_final

  nsamples <- ncol(Joint_S_beta)

  ##########################################################
  # Calculate joint posterior predictive probabilities
  ##########################################################

  estimated_PP <- array(
    NA_real_,
    dim = c(n_test, k1 * k2, nsamples)
  )

  for (iter in seq_len(nsamples)) {

    beta_draw <- Joint_S_beta[, iter]

    # Regression coefficients for response 1
    beta1 <- matrix(
      beta_draw[1:((k1 - 1) * p1)],
      ncol = p1,
      byrow = TRUE
    )

    # Regression coefficients for response 2
    beta2 <- matrix(
      beta_draw[
        (((k1 - 1) * p1) + 1):length(beta_draw)
      ],
      ncol = p2,
      byrow = TRUE
    )

    # Test-set linear predictors
    test_X1_Beta <- x1_test %*% t(beta1)
    test_X2_Beta <- x2_test %*% t(beta2)

    # Joint category probabilities
    estimated_PP[, , iter] <- apply(
      matrix(1:(k1 * k2), ncol = 1),
      1,
      new_probability_mnp_2response,
      k1,
      k2,
      mu1 = test_X1_Beta,
      mu2 = test_X2_Beta,
      sigma = Joint_S_sigma[, , iter],
      r = 250,
      Halton_choice = FALSE
    )
  }

  ##########################################################
  # Store prediction results
  ##########################################################

  estimated_PP_list[[cv]] <- estimated_PP

  test_Y_list[[cv]] <- cbind(
    y1_test,
    y2_test
  )

  cv_response_list[cv] <- job$response
  cv_target_row_list[[cv]] <- target_row

  cat(
    "Completed CV:", cv,
    "of", length(cv_jobs), "\n"
  )
}

############################################################
# 4. Save cross-validation results
############################################################

save(
  estimated_PP_list,
  test_Y_list,
  cv_response_list,
  cv_target_row_list,
  unq_row_of_X_y1,
  unq_row_of_X_y2,
  file = file.path(
    path,
    "Table_7.RData"
  )
)

############################################################
#  Calculate observed proportions and 95% HPD intervals
############################################################

get_table_row <- function(cv) {

  pp <- estimated_PP_list[[cv]]
  yy <- as.matrix(test_Y_list[[cv]])

  resp <- cv_response_list[cv]

  ns <- dim(pp)[3]
  n_test <- dim(pp)[1]

  if (resp == 1L) {

    # Mental illness
    true <- sapply(
      seq_len(k1),
      function(a) mean(yy[, 1] == a)
    )

    draws <- matrix(NA_real_, ns, k1)

    for (a in seq_len(k1)) {

      cols <- ((a - 1) * k2 + 1):(a * k2)

      z <- apply(
        pp[, cols, , drop = FALSE],
        c(1, 3),
        sum
      )

      z <- matrix(z, nrow = n_test, ncol = ns)
      draws[, a] <- colMeans(z)
    }

  } else {

    # Alcohol and drug abuse
    true <- sapply(
      seq_len(k2),
      function(b) mean(yy[, 2] == b)
    )

    draws <- matrix(NA_real_, ns, k2)

    for (b in seq_len(k2)) {

      cols <- seq(b, k1 * k2, by = k2)

      z <- apply(
        pp[, cols, , drop = FALSE],
        c(1, 3),
        sum
      )

      z <- matrix(z, nrow = n_test, ncol = ns)
      draws[, b] <- colMeans(z)
    }
  }

  # 95% HPD predictive intervals
  hp <- t(
    apply(
      draws,
      2,
      function(z) HDInterval::hdi(
        z,
        credMass = 0.95
      )
    )
  )

  list(
    true = true,
    median = apply(draws, 2, median),
    lower = hp[, 1],
    upper = hp[, 2],
    covered = true >= hp[, 1] & true <= hp[, 2]
  )
}

tabres <- lapply(
  seq_along(cv_jobs),
  get_table_row
)


build_table <- function(ids, patterns) {

  if (length(ids) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  K <- length(tabres[[ids[1]]]$true)

  tr <- lo <- up <- med <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    length(ids),
    K
  )

  cov <- matrix(FALSE, length(ids), K)
  disp <- matrix("", length(ids), K)

  for (i in seq_along(ids)) {

    z <- tabres[[ids[i]]]

    tr[i, ] <- z$true
    lo[i, ] <- z$lower
    up[i, ] <- z$upper
    med[i, ] <- z$median
    cov[i, ] <- z$covered

    for (j in seq_len(K)) {

      disp[i, j] <- sprintf(
        "%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)",
        tr[i, j],
        lo[i, j],
        up[i, j]
      )
    }
  }

  colnames(disp) <- paste0(
    "Category ",
    0:(K - 1)
  )

  list(
    covariate_combinations = patterns,
    table = disp,
    true = tr,
    posterior_median = med,
    HPD_lower = lo,
    HPD_upper = up,
    covered = cov
  )
}

id1 <- which(cv_response_list == 1L)
id2 <- which(cv_response_list == 2L)

Mental_Illness_Bivariate <- build_table(
  id1,
  unq_row_of_X_y1
)

Alcohol_Drug_Abuse_Bivariate <- build_table(
  id2,
  unq_row_of_X_y2
)

# Display Table 7
cat("\nMENTAL ILLNESS -- BIVARIATE MODEL\n")

if (!is.null(Mental_Illness_Bivariate)) {

  print(
    Mental_Illness_Bivariate$covariate_combinations
  )

  knitr::kable(
    Mental_Illness_Bivariate$table,
    caption = "Mental illness: observed proportions and 95% HPD predictive intervals"
  )
}

cat("\nALCOHOL & DRUG ABUSE -- BIVARIATE MODEL\n")

if (!is.null(Alcohol_Drug_Abuse_Bivariate)) {

  print(
    Alcohol_Drug_Abuse_Bivariate$covariate_combinations
  )

  knitr::kable(
    Alcohol_Drug_Abuse_Bivariate$table,
    caption = "Alcohol and drug abuse: observed proportions and 95% HPD predictive intervals"
  )
}
```
